categories.main_business_segments: Kyochon F&B operates primarily in three segments: domestic franchise business focusing on chicken franchise under the Kyochon Chicken brand, global business involving direct-operated stores and master franchise operations overseas, and new businesses including distribution of processed foods (HMR), sauces, and craft beer. The domestic franchise segment supplies raw and auxiliary materials to franchisees, while the global segment manages overseas stores and master franchise partnerships. New business initiatives focus on expanding processed food and craft beer markets leveraging brand synergy.
categories.core_technologies_production_methods: The company emphasizes proprietary sauce recipes based on natural ingredients and unique cooking methods such as 21-piece cutting for chicken. Production of sauces and pickled radish is conducted through subsidiaries with dedicated manufacturing facilities. Craft beer production uses premium natural ingredients and traditional brewing techniques, including German-style lagers and unique flavor profiles. The company also invests in R&D for new menu items, sauces, and fermented food products to maintain competitive differentiation.
categories.primary_customers_markets: Primary customers include domestic franchisees operating Kyochon Chicken outlets, overseas franchise partners, and end consumers purchasing processed foods and craft beer through various retail channels. The domestic market is the largest, with franchisees as key customers for raw materials and sauces. Global markets include the US, China, Southeast Asia, Middle East, and Canada through direct and master franchise models. New business customers include retail consumers via online and offline distribution channels.
categories.geographic_coverage: Operations span South Korea as the core domestic market, with global presence in the United States and China through direct-operated stores. Additional international markets such as Malaysia, Indonesia, Thailand, UAE, Taiwan, and Canada are served via master franchise agreements. The company continues to expand its global footprint by selecting markets based on comprehensive market evaluations and partnering with capable local franchisees.
categories.supply_chain_position: Kyochon F&B operates primarily midstream and downstream in the supply chain as a franchisor and distributor. It sources raw chicken and auxiliary materials from external suppliers and its subsidiaries, then supplies these to franchisees. The company also produces some processed foods and sauces internally. In craft beer, it controls production from raw material procurement to finished product sales. The company manages logistics and distribution to franchisees and retail channels.
categories.strategic_focus_rd_direction: Strategic priorities include strengthening franchise profitability, expanding global business rapidly, nurturing the sauce business, and enhancing ESG management. R&D focuses on developing signature menu items, new sauces, fermented foods, and HMR products. Innovation themes include product differentiation through natural ingredients, flavor innovation, and platform development for improved customer engagement. The company invests in education and quality control to maintain competitive advantage.
categories.revenue_model: Revenue is generated mainly through sales of raw and auxiliary materials to franchisees, royalties and fees from master franchise partners, and sales of processed foods and craft beer through retail channels. The global business earns revenue from master franchise fees, royalties on sales, training fees, inspection fees, and exports of sauces and materials. New business revenue comes from processed food and beverage product sales via online and offline distribution.
categories.key_competitors_industry_positioning: Kyochon F&B is positioned as a leading chicken franchise brand in South Korea with a strong domestic market share and recognized brand loyalty. It competes in a highly competitive chicken franchise market with approximately 700 registered brands. The company differentiates through product innovation, quality control, and brand management. Globally, it competes by leveraging direct-operated stores and master franchise models to expand presence. It holds top industry awards and maintains a competitive edge through continuous franchise support and marketing.
categories.financial_scale_growth_profile: As of 2023, the company reported consolidated revenues of approximately 445 billion KRW, with domestic franchise sales comprising 93%, global business 4%, and new businesses 3%. Despite a 14% revenue decline from the prior year due to price adjustments and economic conditions, operating profit increased significantly to 24.8 billion KRW. Total assets reached 326 billion KRW with a stable capital structure. The company has shown consistent growth in franchise numbers and global store count, while investing in new business areas for future growth.
categories.value_proposition_product_differentiatio: Kyochon F&B emphasizes unique natural ingredient-based sauces and differentiated cooking methods to deliver high-quality, flavorful chicken products. Its signature soy garlic, red chili, honey, and black secret sauce series provide distinct taste profiles. The company offers convenient portioned chicken cuts and innovative menu items aligned with consumer trends. Craft beer products complement the chicken brand, enhancing customer experience. Strong franchise support, quality control, and brand loyalty underpin its competitive advantage.
